questions.q:
A quasi-static cycle of a monoatomic ideal gas contains an isothermal process $(\boldsymbol{ab})$, followed by an isochoric process $(\boldsymbol{bc})$ and an adiabatic process $(\boldsymbol{ca})$ as shown in the figure. The volumes of the gas are $V_1$ and $V_2$ at $\boldsymbol{a}$ and $\boldsymbol{b}$, respectively. If the cycle has heat input $Q_{\text{in}}$ and output $Q_{\text{out}}$, then the efficiency of the cycle is defined as $\eta = \dfrac{Q_{\text{in}} - Q_{\text{out}}}{Q_{\text{in}}}$. The correct statement(s) is/are:
[Given: $\ln 2 \approx 0.7$]
options: If $V_2/V_1 = 8$, the heat released in the process $\boldsymbol{bc}$ is smaller than the heat absorbed in the process $\boldsymbol{ab}$.
For a given value of $V_2/V_1$, $\eta$ does not depend on the temperature of the isothermal process.
If $V_2/V_1 = 8$, then the temperature of the gas at $\boldsymbol{a}$ is $4$ times the temperature of the gas at $\boldsymbol{c}$.
If $V_2/V_1 = 8$, then the pressure of the gas at $\boldsymbol{a}$ is $4$ times the pressure of the gas at $\boldsymbol{b}$.
questions.solution:
For the monoatomic ideal gas, $\gamma = \dfrac{5}{3}$.

Process $ab$ is isothermal, so $T_a = T_b$ and $V_a = V_1$, $V_b = V_2$.

Process $bc$ is isochoric, so $V_b = V_c = V_2$.

Process $ca$ is adiabatic, so $T_c V_c^{\gamma-1} = T_a V_a^{\gamma-1}$.

$T_c V_2^{2/3} = T_a V_1^{2/3} \Rightarrow T_c = T_a \left(\dfrac{V_1}{V_2}\right)^{2/3}$.

If $\dfrac{V_2}{V_1} = 8$, $T_c = T_a \left(\dfrac{1}{8}\right)^{2/3} = \dfrac{T_a}{4} \Rightarrow T_a = 4 T_c$. Thus, statement (C) is correct.

Heat absorbed in isothermal process $ab$ is $Q_{ab} = nRT_a \ln\left(\dfrac{V_2}{V_1}\right)$.

For $\dfrac{V_2}{V_1} = 8$, $Q_{ab} = nRT_a \ln(8) = 3nRT_a \ln 2 \approx 3 \times 0.7 nRT_a = 2.1 nRT_a$.

Heat released in isochoric process $bc$ is $Q_{bc} = nC_v(T_b - T_c) = n\left(\dfrac{3}{2}R\right)\left(T_a - \dfrac{T_a}{4}\right) = \dfrac{9}{8}nRT_a = 1.125 nRT_a$.

Since $1.125 nRT_a < 2.1 nRT_a$, the heat released in $bc$ is smaller than the heat absorbed in $ab$. Thus, statement (A) is correct.

The efficiency of the cycle is $\eta = 1 - \dfrac{Q_{\text{out}}}{Q_{\text{in}}} = 1 - \dfrac{Q_{bc}}{Q_{ab}}$.

$\eta = 1 - \dfrac{n \left(\dfrac{3}{2} R\right) T_a \left(1 - \left(\dfrac{V_1}{V_2}\right)^{2/3}\right)}{nRT_a \ln\left(\dfrac{V_2}{V_1}\right)} = 1 - \dfrac{3 \left(1 - \left(\dfrac{V_1}{V_2}\right)^{2/3}\right)}{2 \ln\left(\dfrac{V_2}{V_1}\right)}$.

This expression depends only on the volume ratio $\dfrac{V_2}{V_1}$ and is independent of the temperature $T_a$. Thus, statement (B) is correct.

For the isothermal process $ab$, $P_a V_a = P_b V_b \Rightarrow P_a V_1 = P_b V_2 \Rightarrow P_a = 8 P_b$. Thus, statement (D) is incorrect.

Answer: If $V_2/V_1 = 8$, the heat released in the process $\boldsymbol{bc}$ is smaller than the heat absorbed in the process $\boldsymbol{ab}$.; For a given value of $V_2/V_1$, $\eta$ does not depend on the temperature of the isothermal process.; If $V_2/V_1 = 8$, then the temperature of the gas at $\boldsymbol{a}$ is $4$ times the temperature of the gas at $\boldsymbol{c}$.

questions.q: As shown in the figure, five Carnot engines, each with efficiency $\eta$ and same number of cycles per unit time, are operating between six heat reservoirs. The amount of heat released per cycle by one engine is completely absorbed by the next engine. Consider $Q_0$ to be the amount of heat absorbed per cycle by the first engine and $W$ as the amount of total work done by all the engines per cycle, then the net efficiency of the system is found to be $\eta_{\text{net}} = \dfrac{W}{Q_0} = \dfrac{211}{243}$. The value of $\eta$ is:
questions.solution:
Let $Q_0$ be the heat absorbed by the first engine and $Q_1$ be the heat rejected.

The efficiency of the first engine is $\eta = 1 - \dfrac{Q_1}{Q_0} \Rightarrow Q_1 = Q_0(1 - \eta)$

Similarly, for the second engine, the heat rejected is $Q_2 = Q_1(1 - \eta) = Q_0(1 - \eta)^2$

Following this pattern, for the $5^{\text{th}}$ engine, the heat rejected is $Q_5 = Q_0(1 - \eta)^5$

The total work done by all five engines is $W = W_1 + W_2 + W_3 + W_4 + W_5 = (Q_0 - Q_1) + (Q_1 - Q_2) + \dots + (Q_4 - Q_5) = Q_0 - Q_5$

The net efficiency of the system is $\eta_{\text{net}} = \dfrac{W}{Q_0} = \dfrac{Q_0 - Q_5}{Q_0} = 1 - \dfrac{Q_5}{Q_0}$

Substituting the value of $Q_5$, we get $\eta_{\text{net}} = 1 - (1 - \eta)^5$

Given $\eta_{\text{net}} = \dfrac{211}{243}$

$1 - (1 - \eta)^5 = \dfrac{211}{243}$

$(1 - \eta)^5 = 1 - \dfrac{211}{243} = \dfrac{32}{243}$

$(1 - \eta)^5 = \left(\dfrac{2}{3}\right)^5$

$1 - \eta = \dfrac{2}{3}$

$\eta = \dfrac{1}{3}$

Answer: $0.33$

questions.q:
Ten moles of an ideal monoatomic gas, initially in state $\boldsymbol{a}$ at atmospheric pressure and temperature $T_a = 27^\circ$C, is enclosed in a metal cylinder of volume $V_0$ fitted with a frictionless piston. The gas is suddenly compressed to state $\boldsymbol{b}$ with volume $V_0/3$. Now, keeping the piston stationary, the cylinder is submerged in a water bath of temperature $11^\circ$C until the gas reaches the temperature of the water bath, which is denoted as state $\boldsymbol{c}$. Finally, while still in the water bath, the piston is brought slowly to its initial position, which is denoted as state $\boldsymbol{f}$. If $R$ is universal gas constant, then the correct option(s) is/are:
[Given: $9^{1/3} = 2.08$]
options: The schematic P-V diagram of the processes described above is:
The change in internal energy in going from state $\boldsymbol{a}$ to $\boldsymbol{b}$ is $4860R$.
The net change in the internal energy in the whole process is $-240R$.
The pressure and temperature of the state $\boldsymbol{b}$ are $2.08$ times the atmospheric pressure and $624$ K, respectively.
questions.solution:
For state $a$: $n = 10$, $T_a = 27^{\circ}\text{C} = 300\text{ K}$, $P_a = 1\text{ atm}$, $V_a = V_0$.
For a monoatomic gas, $C_v = \dfrac{3}{2}R$ and $\gamma = \dfrac{5}{3}$.

Process $a \rightarrow b$ is a sudden compression, which is an adiabatic process.
$V_b = \dfrac{V_0}{3}$
Using $T_a V_a^{\gamma-1} = T_b V_b^{\gamma-1}$:
$T_b = T_a \left(\dfrac{V_a}{V_b}\right)^{\gamma-1} = 300 \times (3)^{5/3 - 1} = 300 \times 3^{2/3} = 300 \times (9)^{1/3}$
Given $9^{1/3} = 2.08$, we get $T_b = 300 \times 2.08 = 624\text{ K}$.
Using $P_a V_a^\gamma = P_b V_b^\gamma$:
$P_b = P_a \left(\dfrac{V_a}{V_b}\right)^\gamma = 1 \times (3)^{5/3} = 3 \times 3^{2/3} = 3 \times 2.08 = 6.24\text{ atm}$.
Thus, the pressure at state $b$ is $6.24$ times the atmospheric pressure. Option (D) is incorrect.

The change in internal energy for process $a \rightarrow b$ is:
$\Delta U_{ab} = n C_v (T_b - T_a) = 10 \times \dfrac{3}{2}R \times (624 - 300) = 15R \times 324 = 4860R$.
Option (B) is correct.

Process $b \rightarrow c$ is isochoric (stationary piston), so $V_c = \dfrac{V_0}{3}$.
The gas cools to the water bath temperature, $T_c = 11^{\circ}\text{C} = 284\text{ K}$.

Process $c \rightarrow f$ is isothermal (slow expansion in water bath), so $T_f = T_c = 284\text{ K}$ and $V_f = V_0$.
The net change in internal energy for the entire process $a \rightarrow f$ depends only on the initial and final temperatures:
$\Delta U_{net} = n C_v (T_f - T_a) = 10 \times \dfrac{3}{2}R \times (284 - 300) = 15R \times (-16) = -240R$.
Option (C) is correct.

For the P-V diagram:
Process $a \rightarrow b$ is an adiabatic compression (curve upwards and to the left).
Process $b \rightarrow c$ is an isochoric cooling (vertical line downwards).
Process $c \rightarrow f$ is an isothermal expansion (curve downwards and to the right).
Comparing pressures at volume $V_0$:
$P_a = \dfrac{nR(300)}{V_0}$ and $P_f = \dfrac{nR(284)}{V_0}$
Since $P_a > P_f$, point $a$ lies above point $f$. The given schematic diagram correctly represents all these features. Option (A) is correct.

Answer: The schematic P-V diagram of the processes described above is: ; The change in internal energy in going from state $\boldsymbol{a}$ to $\boldsymbol{b}$ is $4860R$.; The net change in the internal energy in the whole process is $-240R$.

questions.q: The efficiency of a Carnot engine operating with a hot reservoir kept at a temperature of 1000 K is 0.4. It extracts 150 J of heat per cycle from the hot reservoir. The work extracted from this engine is being fully used to run a heat pump which has a coefficient of performance 10 . The hot reservoir of the heat pump is at a temperature of 300 K . Which of the following statements is/are correct:
options: Work extracted from the Carnot engine in one cycle is 60 J .
Temperature of the cold reservoir of the Carnot engine is 600 K .
Temperature of the cold reservoir of the heat pump is 270 K .
Heat supplied to the hot reservoir of the heat pump in one cycle is 540 J .

The volume of the gas at $W, X$ and $Y$ points are, $64 \mathrm{~cm}^3, 125 \mathrm{~cm}^3$ and $250 \mathrm{~cm}^3$, respectively. If the absolute temperature of the gas $T_W$ at the point $W$ is such that $n R T_W=1 \mathrm{~J}$ ( R is the universal gas constant), then the amount of heat absorbed (in J ) by the gas along the path $X Y$ is $\qquad$

$\begin{aligned}
& \mathrm{nRT}_{\mathrm{W}}=\mathrm{P}_{\mathrm{W}} \mathrm{ V}_{\mathrm{W}}=1 \mathrm{ J} \\
& \mathrm{P}_{\mathrm{W}}=\frac{1}{64} \times 10^6 \mathrm{ Pa}
\end{aligned}$
For WX process
$\begin{aligned}
& P_X V_X^Y=P_W V_W^y \\
& \Rightarrow P_X=P_W\left(\frac{V_W}{V_X}\right)^y
\end{aligned}$
amount of heat absorbed in XY process

questions.q: One mole of an ideal gas undergoes two different cyclic processes $I$ and $II$, as shown in the $P - V$ diagrams below. In cycle $I$, processes $a, b, c$ and $d$ are isobaric, isothermal, isobaric and isochoric, respectively. In cycle $II$, processes $a ' , b ' , c '$ and $d '$ are isothermal, isochoric, isobaric and isochoric, respectively. The total work done during cycle $I$ is ${W}_{I}$ and that during cycle $II$ is ${W}_{II}$. The ratio $\dfrac{{W}_{I}}{{W}_{II}}$ is _____.
questions.solution:
For first case:

${W}_{I} = {W}_{a} + {W}_{b} + {W}_{c} + {W}_{d}$

$= 4{P}_{0}\left(2{V}_{0} - {V}_{0}\right) + nRTln\left(\dfrac{4{V}_{0}}{2{V}_{0}}\right) + 2{P}_{0}\left({V}_{0} - 4{V}_{0}\right) + 0$

$= 4{P}_{0}{V}_{0} + nR\left(\dfrac{8{P}_{0}{V}_{0}}{nR}\right)ln2 - 6{P}_{0}{V}_{0}$

$= 8{P}_{0}{V}_{0}ln2 - 2{P}_{0}{V}_{0}$

For second case:

${W}_{II} = W{'}_{a} + W{'}_{b} + W{'}_{c} + W{'}_{d}$

$= nRTln\left(\dfrac{2{V}_{0}}{{V}_{0}}\right) + 0 + {P}_{0}\left({V}_{0} - 2{V}_{0}\right) + 0$

$= nR\left(\dfrac{4{P}_{0}{V}_{0}}{nR}\right)ln2 - {P}_{0}{V}_{0}$

$= 4{P}_{0}{V}_{0}ln2 - {P}_{0}{V}_{0}$

Therefore, required ratio is $\dfrac{{W}_{I}}{{W}_{II}} = \dfrac{8{P}_{0}{V}_{0}ln2 - 2{P}_{0}{V}_{0}}{4{P}_{0}{V}_{0}ln2 - {P}_{0}{V}_{0}} = 2$

questions.q: A closed container contains a homogeneous mixture of two moles of an ideal monatomic gas $\left(\gamma = \dfrac{5}{3}\right)$ and one mole of an ideal diatomic gas $\left(\gamma = \dfrac{7}{5}\right)$. Here, $\gamma$ is the ratio of the specific heats at constant pressure and constant volume of an ideal gas. The gas mixture does a work of $66$ Joule when heated at constant pressure. The change in its internal energy is _____ Joule.
questions.solution:
Change in internal energy for the mixture can be written as,$∆ U = {n}_{1}{\left({C}_{v}\right)}_{1} ∆ T + {n}_{2}{\left({C}_{v}\right)}_{2} ∆ T$

$= \left({n}_{1}{\left({C}_{v}\right)}_{1} + {n}_{2}{\left({C}_{v}\right)}_{2}\right) ∆ T . . . \left(i\right)$

For isobaric process, work done $= P ∆ V$

$= \left({n}_{1} + {n}_{2}\right)R ∆ T . . . \left(ii\right)$

Divide $\left(i\right)$ by $\left(ii\right)$, we get

$\dfrac{∆ U}{W} = \dfrac{\left({n}_{1}{\left({C}_{v}\right)}_{1} + {n}_{2}{\left({C}_{v}\right)}_{2}\right) ∆ T}{\left({n}_{1} + {n}_{2}\right)R ∆ T}$

$⇒ ∆ U = \dfrac{W}{R}\left(\dfrac{\left({n}_{1}{\left({C}_{v}\right)}_{1} + {n}_{2}{\left({C}_{v}\right)}_{2}\right)}{{n}_{1} + {n}_{2}}\right)$

$= \dfrac{66}{R}\dfrac{\left[2 \times \dfrac{3R}{2} + 1 \times \dfrac{5R}{2}\right]}{2 + 1}$

$= 121J$

An ideal gas of density $ρ = 0 . 2kg{m}^{- 3}$ enters a chimney of height $h$ at the rate of $\alpha = 0 . 8kg{s}^{- 1}$ from its lower end, and escapes through the upper end as shown in the figure. The cross-sectional area of the lower end is ${A}_{1} = 0 . 1{m}^{2}$ and the upper end is ${A}_{2} = 0 . 4{m}^{2}$. The pressure and the temperature of the gas at the lower end are $600Pa$ and $300K$, respectively, while its temperature at the upper end is $150K$. The chimney is heat insulated so that the gas undergoes adiabatic expansion. Take $g = 10m{s}^{- 2}$ and the ratio of specific heats of the gas $\gamma = 2$. Ignore atmospheric pressure.

Which of the following statement(s) is(are) correct?
options: The pressure of the gas at the upper end of the chimney is $300Pa$.
The velocity of the gas at the lower end of the chimney is $40m{s}^{- 1}$ and at the upper end is $20m{s}^{- 1}$.
The height of the chimney is $590m$.
The density of the gas at the upper end is $0 . 05kg{m}^{- 3}$.
questions.solution:
Here the gas undergoes adiabatic expansion,

${P}^{1 - \gamma}{T}^{\gamma} =$constant

$⇒ \dfrac{{P}_{2}}{{P}_{1}} = \left(\dfrac{{T}_{1}}{{T}_{2}}\right)\dfrac{\gamma}{1 - \gamma}$

$⇒ {P}_{2} = \left(\dfrac{300}{150}\right)\dfrac{2}{1 - 2} \times 600$

$⇒ {P}_{2} = \dfrac{600}{4} = 150Pa$

Thus, pressure of the gas at the upper end of the chimney is ${P}_{2} = 150Pa$

From ideal gas equation, $ρ = \dfrac{PM}{RT} ⇒ ρ ∝ \dfrac{P}{T}$

Then, $\dfrac{{ρ}_{1}}{{ρ}_{2}} = \left(\dfrac{{P}_{1}}{{P}_{2}}\right)\left(\dfrac{{T}_{1}}{{T}_{2}}\right) = \left(\dfrac{150}{600}\right)\left(\dfrac{300}{150}\right) = \dfrac{1}{2}$

$⇒ {ρ}_{2} = \left(0 . 2\right)\dfrac{1}{2} = 0 . 1kg{m}^{- 3}$

Rate of mass flow $\alpha = 0 . 8kg{s}^{- 1}$

$⇒$ Volume flow rate at top $= \dfrac{0 . 8}{0 . 1} = 8{m}^{3}{s}^{- 1}$

Velocity of gas at lower end ${v}_{1} = \dfrac{{V}_{1}}{{A}_{1}} = \dfrac{0 . 8}{0 . 2 \times 0 . 1} = 40m{s}^{- 1}$

Velocity of gas at upper end ${v}_{2} = \dfrac{0 . 8 \times 2}{0 . 2 \times 0 . 4} = 20m{s}^{- 1}$

Work done ${W}_{ongas} = ∆ K + ∆ {U}_{g} + \text{internal energy}$

${P}_{1}{A}_{1} ∆ {x}_{1} - {P}_{2}{A}_{2} ∆ {x}_{2} = \dfrac{1}{2} ∆ m{{v}_{1}}^{2} - \dfrac{1}{2} ∆ m{{v}_{2}}^{2} + mg ∆ h + \dfrac{f}{2}\left({P}_{2} ∆ {V}_{2} - {P}_{1} ∆ {V}_{1}\right)$

Solving we get $h = 360m$

List I describes thermodynamic processes in four different systems. List II gives the magnitudes (either exactly or as a close approximation) of possible changes in the internal energy of the system due to the process.

List-I List-II
(I) ${10}^{- 3}kg$ of water $100 ° C$ is converted to steam at the same temperature, at a pressure of ${10}^{5}Pa$. The volume of the system changes from ${10}^{- 6}{m}^{3}$ to ${10}^{- 3}{m}^{3}$ in the process. Latent heat of water $= 2250kJ{kg}^{- 1}$ (P) $2kJ$
(II) $0 . 2$ moles of a rigid diatomic ideal gas with volume $V$ at temperature $500K$ undergoes an isobaric expansion to volume $3V$. Assume $8 . 0J{mol}^{– 1}{K}^{– 1}$ (Q) $7kJ$
(III) One mole of a monoatomic ideal gas is compressed adiabatically from volume $V = \dfrac{1}{3}{m}^{3}$ and pressure $2kPa$ to volume $\dfrac{V}{8}$. (R) $4kJ$
(IV) Three moles of a diatomic ideal gas whose molecules can vibrate, is given $9kJ$ of heat and undergoes isobaric expansion. (S) $5kJ$
(T) $3kJ$

Which one of the following options is correct?
options: $I \to T, II \to R, III \to S, IV \to Q$
$I \to S, II \to P, III \to T, IV \to P$
$I \to P, II \to R, III \to T, IV \to Q$
$I \to Q, II \to R, III \to S, IV \to T$
questions.solution:
(I)

According to the first law of thermodynamics,

$∆ Q = ∆ U + W ⇒ ∆ U = ∆ Q - W$

$⇒ U = ML - P\DeltaV$

$= {10}^{- 3} \times 2250 - {10}^{2}kP \times \left({10}^{- 3} - {10}^{- 6}\right){m}^{3}$

$= 2 . 25kJ - 0 . 1kJ$

$= 2 . 15kJ$

Therefore, I-P

(II)

For isobaric process,

$\dfrac{{V}_{1}}{{V}_{2}} = \dfrac{{T}_{1}}{{T}_{2}} ⇒ {T}_{2} = 3 \times 500 = 1500K$

Now the change in the internal energy will be,

$∆ U = n{C}_{V} ∆ T = 0 . 2 \times \dfrac{5}{2} \times 8 \times 1000 = 4kJ$

Therefore, II-R

(III)

For adiabatic expansion of monoatomic gas $\left(\gamma = \dfrac{5}{3}\right)$

${P}_{1}{V}_{1}^{\gamma} = {P}_{2}{V}_{2}^{\gamma} ⇒ \left(2kPa\right) \times {V}_{0}^{\dfrac{5}{3}} = {P}_{2} \times \left(\dfrac{{V}_{0}}{8}\right)\dfrac{5}{3}$

$⇒ {P}_{2} = 64kPa$

Now the change in the internal energy will be,

$\DeltaU = n{C}_{v}\DeltaT$

$= \dfrac{3nR\DeltaT}{2} = \dfrac{3}{2}\left({P}_{2}{V}_{2} - {P}_{1}{V}_{1}\right) = \dfrac{3}{2} \times \left(64 \times \dfrac{1}{3 \times 8} - 2 \times \dfrac{1}{3}\right)$

$= \dfrac{3}{2} \times \left(\dfrac{8}{3} - \dfrac{2}{3}\right) = 3kJ$

Therefore, III-T

(IV)

For diatomic gas whose molecules vibrate,

${C}_{V} = \dfrac{6}{2}R$ and ${C}_{P} = \dfrac{8}{2}R$

$⇒ \DeltaU = n{C}_{V}\DeltaT = 3nR\DeltaT$

$\DeltaQ = n{C}_{p}\DeltaT = 4nR\DeltaT$

$\dfrac{\DeltaU}{\DeltaQ} = \dfrac{3}{4}$

$\DeltaU = \dfrac{3}{4} \times 9 = 6 . 75 ≃ 7kJ$

Therefore, IV-Q

questions.solution:
Writing ${C}_{V}$ in terms of degree of freedom of the gas $f$, we get,

${C}_{V} = \dfrac{f}{2}R = 2R ⇒ f = 4,$

Therefore,​ adiabatic index of gas will be given by,​​​​​​$\gamma = 1 + \dfrac{2}{f} = 1 + \dfrac{2}{4} = \dfrac{3}{2}$

$⇒ {T}_{R} = \sqrt{2}{T}_{0} ⇒ \dfrac{{T}_{R}}{{T}_{0}} = \sqrt{2}$

The gas is then heated very slowly to temperature ${T}_{2}$ , pressure ${P}_{2}$ and volume ${V}_{2}$ . During this process the piston moves out by a distance $x$ . Ignoring the friction between the piston the cylinder, the correct statement(s) is (are)
options: If  ${V}_{2} = 2{V}_{1}$  and  ${T}_{2} = 3{T}_{1}$ , then the energy stored in the spring is  $\dfrac{1}{4}{P}_{1}{V}_{1}$
If  ${V}_{2} = 2{V}_{1}$  and  ${T}_{2} = 3{T}_{1}$ , then the change in internal energy is  $3{P}_{1}{V}_{1}$
If  ${V}_{2} = 3{V}_{1}$  and  ${T}_{2} = 4{T}_{1}$ , then the work done by the gas is  $\dfrac{7}{3}{P}_{1}{V}_{1}$
If  ${V}_{2} = 3{V}_{1}$  and  ${T}_{2} = 4{T}_{1}$ , then the heat supplied to the gas is  $\dfrac{17}{6}{P}_{1}{V}_{1}$

(i) $P = {P}_{1} + \dfrac{Kx}{A}$
${P}_{2} = \dfrac{3}{2}{P}_{1} ⇒ x = \dfrac{{V}_{1}}{A}$
$\dfrac{3{P}_{1}}{2} = {P}_{1} + \dfrac{Kx}{A}$
$Kx = \dfrac{{P}_{1}A}{2}$
Energy of spring
$\dfrac{1}{2}K{x}^{2} = \dfrac{{P}_{1}A}{4}x = \dfrac{{P}_{1}{V}_{1}}{4}$
(ii) $∆ U = \dfrac{f}{2}\left({P}_{2}{V}_{2} - {P}_{2}{V}_{1}\right)$
$= 3{P}_{1}{V}_{1}$
(iii) ${P}_{f} = \dfrac{4{P}_{1}}{3}$
$KX = \dfrac{{P}_{1}}{3}A$
$X = \dfrac{2{V}_{1}}{A}$
${W}_{gas} = - \left({W}_{{P}_{atm}} + {W}_{spring}\right)$
$= \left({P}_{1}Ax + \dfrac{1}{2}Kx . x\right)$
$= + \left({P}_{1}A . \dfrac{2{V}_{1}}{A} + \dfrac{1}{2} . \dfrac{{P}_{1}A}{3} . \dfrac{2{V}_{1}}{A}\right)$
$= 2{P}_{1}{V}_{1} + \dfrac{{P}_{1}{V}_{1}}{3} = \dfrac{7{P}_{1}{V}_{1}}{3}$
(iv) $∆ Q = W + ∆ U$
$= \dfrac{7{P}_{1}{V}_{1}}{3} + \dfrac{3}{2}\left({P}_{2}{V}_{2} - {P}_{1}{V}_{1}\right)$
$= \dfrac{7{P}_{1}{V}_{1}}{3} + \dfrac{3}{2}\left(\dfrac{4}{3}{P}_{1} . 3{V}_{1} - {P}_{1}{V}_{1}\right)$
$= \dfrac{7{P}_{1}{V}_{1}}{3} + \dfrac{9}{2}{P}_{1}{V}_{1} = \dfrac{41{P}_{1}{V}_{1}}{6}$

Paragraph: In the figure a container is shown to have a movable (without friction) piston on top. The container and the piston are all made of perfectly insulating material allowing no heat transfer between outside and inside the container. The container is divided into two compartments by a rigid partition made of a thermally conducting material that allows slow transfer of heat. The lower compartment of the container is filled with $2$ moles of an ideal monatomic gas at $700 K$ and the upper compartment is filled with $2$ moles of an ideal diatomic gas at $400 K$. The heat capacities per mole of an ideal monatomic gas are $C_{V}=\frac{3}{2} R, C_{P}=\frac{5}{2} R$, and those for an ideal diatomic gas are $C_{V}=\frac{5}{2} R, C_{P}=\frac{7}{2} R$.

Question: Consider the partition to be rigidly fixed so that it does not move. When equilibrium is achieved, the final temperature of the gases will be
questions.solution:
Heat given by lower compartment $= 2 \times \dfrac{3}{2}R \times \left(700 - T\right)$ ...(i)
Heat obtained by upper compartment $= 2 \times \dfrac{7}{2}R \times \left(T - 400\right)$ ...(ii)


Equating (i) and (ii)
$3\left(700 - T\right) = 7\left(T - 400\right)$
$2100 - 3T = 7T - 2800$
$4900 = 10T ⇒ T = 490K$

&
